# NimBLE syscfg to Kconfig

NimBLE configures itself through `syscfg.yml` files that Apache newt compiles
into a per-target `syscfg.h`. PebbleOS used to carry one such header per SoC,
generated by hand from a dummy newt project. `gen_syscfg.py` replaces that: it
reads NimBLE's own `syscfg.yml` files and writes

- `../Kconfig.<area>`, one file per group of NimBLE packages, and
- `../port/include/syscfg/syscfg.h`, which defines every `MYNEWT_VAL_<NAME>`
  from the matching Kconfig symbol.

Every NimBLE option is therefore a normal PebbleOS setting, and per-SoC values
live in `soc/<soc>/Kconfig.defconfig` next to everything else.

## Running it

```shell
python3 third_party/nimble/scripts/gen_syscfg.py
```

Run it after bumping the `mynewt-nimble` submodule, and commit the result.
`--check` exits non-zero when the checked-in output is stale, without writing;
the `nimble-syscfg` compliance job runs it on every pull request. `--verbose`
lists the options that stayed out of Kconfig and the values aimed at packages
PebbleOS does not build.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `gen_syscfg.py` | the generator |
| `config.yml` | which packages are converted, how they are grouped, and the few options that need a hand-written shape |
| `booleans.yml` | the options that are flags rather than numbers |
| `port.yml`, `port_nrf.yml` | the apache-mynewt-core options NimBLE's porting layer reads, in `syscfg.yml` format |

## How options are mapped

An option named `FOO` becomes `CONFIG_NIMBLE_FOO`, and the header defines
`MYNEWT_VAL_FOO` from it. The Kconfig type comes from the shape of NimBLE's
`value`:

| `value` | Kconfig | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| an integer | `int` | `BLE_MAX_CONNECTIONS: 1` |
| `0x…` | `hex` | `BLE_LL_PUBLIC_DEV_ADDR: 0x000000000000` |
| `"…"` | `string` | `BLE_SVC_GAP_DEVICE_NAME: '"nimble"'` |
| a `choices:` list | `choice` | `BLE_TRANSPORT_LL: socket` |
| another option | that option's type, defaulting to it | `BLE_GATT_READ: MYNEWT_VAL_BLE_ROLE_CENTRAL` |
| a boolean formula over options | `default 1 if <formula>` | `BLE_GATT_NOTIFY_MULTIPLE: '(MYNEWT_VAL_BLE_VERSION >= 52)'` |

## Flags and numbers

syscfg has no boolean type, and an option's value does not say which it is:
plenty of counts default to 1 (`BLE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`,
`BLE_L2CAP_SIG_MAX_PROCS`). Nothing in NimBLE's own files distinguishes the
two, so `booleans.yml` records the judgement by hand; everything not listed is
an `int`. Setting an int from a defconfig reads `CONFIG_NIMBLE_BLE_SM_LVL=4`,
the same value NimBLE's own documentation quotes.

Deriving the list instead, by reading how the C sources use each option, was
tried and dropped. It worked, but it is a heuristic over code the submodule
owns: a bump can silently reclassify an option, and the answer depends on
details like whether an option is reached through a `#define` alias or
assigned to a plain variable rather than a bitfield. A list that has to be
reviewed when it changes is worth more than one that changes by itself.

The generator rejects an entry it can *disprove* from NimBLE's own files: one
naming an option that no longer exists, one whose option has a `range:` or a
value other than 0 or 1, and one that any `syscfg.yml` in the tree -- apps,
targets, test setups and all -- assigns something else. It cannot prove an
entry right, so adding one means checking how the option is used.

An option whose value is just another option's (`BLE_GATT_READ` is
`MYNEWT_VAL_BLE_ROLE_CENTRAL`) follows that option's type and needs no entry.

## Prompts

A Kconfig prompt comes from the option's description: its opening sentence,
minus the boilerplate NimBLE tends to start with ("This option enables the
...") and any trailing "(0/1)". Where that is missing or too long to read as a
label, the option's own name is spelled out instead. The syscfg name stays in
the Kconfig symbol either way, so `BLE_ROLE_CENTRAL` still finds it.

`syscfg.vals` blocks, including the conditional `syscfg.vals.<expr>` form,
become extra `default … if …` lines ahead of the option's own default, which
reproduces newt's precedence. `syscfg.defs.<expr>` blocks become `depends on`.
`restrictions` have no Kconfig equivalent and are reproduced in the help text.

An option whose value is arithmetic (`BLE_L2CAP_MAX_CHANS: 3*MYNEWT_VAL_…`) or
a plain C macro gets no Kconfig symbol, because Kconfig cannot express the
default; the header keeps NimBLE's expression, and the generator lists what it
skipped. To make such an option configurable anyway, give it an `enum` in
`config.yml`: that turns it into a Kconfig choice whose members map to C
expressions, as `BLE_SM_IO_CAP` does.

## Areas

Each area in `config.yml` groups packages into one `Kconfig.<id>`, and may
carry a `depends` naming the builds that compile them (for instance, only
`BT_HCI_NRF52` builds the link layer). Where that dependency is false, the
area's options take 0, the same value NimBLE sees for a package a newt target
leaves out. The area menu uses `visible if` rather than `if`, because `if`
would also gate the `default` lines and leave the options valueless — which
Kconfig compares as a string, making `SYM != 0` true.

Within a file, NimBLE's own `# … settings.` banner comments become menus.

## Checking a submodule bump

The generated header should keep the options the firmware reads at the values
newt produced. Preprocess a probe listing every `MYNEWT_VAL_*` against the old
header and against the new one plus the build's `autoconf.h`, and compare:

```shell
arm-none-eabi-gcc -E -P -Iold/include probe.c
arm-none-eabi-gcc -E -P -include build/autoconf.h \
    -Ithird_party/nimble/port/include probe.c
```
